verdict.summary: ServiceNow OAuth is per instance. An admin creates an OAuth client in the instance under System OAuth > Application Registry, and nobody at ServiceNow has to approve it. The catch is that every customer instance needs its own registration. Review applies only if you choose the optional ServiceNow Store route, which requires Build Partner membership and certification that ServiceNow's KB says typically takes 3-5 weeks.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 20-45 min per instance; Store listing route is multiple days of documentation and partner enrollment
verdict.time_to_first_connection: 15-30 min (once you have an instance with admin access)
verdict.approval_wait: none for per-instance OAuth; 3-5 weeks (official KB) to 5-8 weeks (reported) only if listing on the ServiceNow Store

gates.name: Application Registry client on your own instance
gates.unlocks: You can connect your own ServiceNow user on your own instance (for example a free personal developer instance) through Composio.
limits: Access token lifespan defaults to 1800 seconds (30 min)
A refresh token is only issued if Refresh Token Lifespan is set above 0 (default 8,640,000 s = 100 days)
Only Authorization Code and Resource Owner Password grants are supported for inbound OAuth (per community source)

gates.name: Other users on the same instance
gates.unlocks: Any user with an account on that instance can authorize through the same registry record. There is no test-user allowlist and no review.
limits: Limited to users of that single instance
Same token lifespans as Gate 1 (30 min access, 100-day refresh by default, both adjustable)
A community thread reports token failures until the user account had 'Web service access only' checked

gates.name: Per-customer instance registration (optional: ServiceNow Store listing)
gates.unlocks: Users on any customer's instance can connect once that instance's admin creates an Application Registry record with your redirect URL. Separately, a Store listing lets customers install a packaged app, but you need Build Partner membership and Store certification for that.
limits: Endpoints are per instance (https://{subdomain}.service-now.com/oauth_auth.do), so each customer needs its own client ID/secret
Store route only: Build Partner membership (annual fee; $5,000 USD in an older official guide, amount unclear after the 2026 changes)
Store route only: app must be in a private scope, pass the Certification Self-Test Tool, and pass app review and listing review
gates.time_to_reach: Per-instance: minutes of admin work for each customer. Store: 3-5 weeks of certification (official KB), 5-8 weeks from build completion (third-party estimate), plus partner enrollment.

steps.title: Get a ServiceNow instance with admin rights
steps.detail: Sign in at developer.servicenow.com and request a free personal developer instance, or use an existing instance where you have admin rights. Note the instance subdomain (the part before .service-now.com). Composio needs it.
gotchas: The developer portal needs JavaScript and a supported browser.

steps.title: Confirm inbound OAuth is enabled
steps.detail: Check that the OAuth 2.0 plugin is active and that the system property com.snc.platform.security.oauth.is.active is set to true (under System Properties). The plugin is on by default on new and upgraded instances. If it is missing, an admin has to activate it.

steps.title: Create a Composio OAUTH2 auth config and copy its callback URL
steps.detail: In Composio, create an auth config for the servicenow toolkit using your own OAuth credentials (OAUTH2 mode; Composio offers no managed app). Copy the callback URL Composio shows; it goes into ServiceNow in the next step. Composio calls https://{subdomain}.service-now.com/oauth_auth.do and /oauth_token.do with default scope useraccount.

steps.title: Create the Application Registry record
steps.detail: In the instance, go to System OAuth > Application Registry, click New, and choose 'Create an OAuth API endpoint for external clients'. Enter a name. Leave Client Secret blank so the instance generates it.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The redirect URL has to match exactly, including scheme and trailing slash.

steps.title: Set token lifespans so you get a refresh token
steps.detail: On the same record, set Refresh Token Lifespan above 0. The default is 8,640,000 seconds (100 days). If it is 0, no refresh token is issued and connections stop after the access token expires. Access Token Lifespan defaults to 1800 seconds and can be raised. Save the record.
gotchas: From the Yokohama release there is also an 'Extend Refresh Token Expiry' field. It mainly matters for outbound integrations.

steps.title: Paste Client ID, Client Secret and subdomain into Composio
steps.detail: Reopen the saved registry record and copy the auto-generated Client ID and Client Secret into your Composio auth config, along with the instance subdomain. The secret is required at the token exchange.

steps.title: Run a test authorization
steps.detail: Start a Composio connection. The flow redirects to oauth_auth.do with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri and state, then exchanges the code at oauth_token.do. Make one REST call to confirm the token works.
gotchas: If no token comes back, a community thread reports it was fixed by checking 'Web service access only' on the user account.
Client credentials grant is not supported for inbound OAuth (per community source). Use authorization code.

steps.title: Let other users on the instance connect
steps.detail: Other users of the same instance can authorize through the same registry record with no extra approval. Have one user complete a connection and confirm their ServiceNow roles allow the API calls your agent makes.

steps.title: Register the client in each customer instance
steps.detail: OAuth clients are per instance, so each customer admin repeats the registry steps (System OAuth > Application Registry > Create an OAuth API endpoint for external clients) in their own instance. An agent can draft a short admin guide with the exact redirect URL, Auth scope useraccount and lifespan settings. In Composio, each customer instance needs its own client credentials and subdomain.

steps.title: (Optional, Store route) Join the Partner Program as a Build Partner
steps.detail: Only do this if you want a ServiceNow Store listing. Create a partner account, submit an application, and wait for application review. Membership has an annual fee. In 2026 ServiceNow added an Access Tier that lets entry-stage partners start building before full enrollment.

steps.title: (Optional, Store route) Build in a private scope and run the self-test
steps.detail: Build the app in a private application scope on your vendor instance. Global-scope apps cannot be published to the Store. Run the Certification Self-Test Tool plugin, then fix or document every finding.

steps.title: (Optional, Store route) Prepare certification documents
steps.detail: Draft the design document and test plan with results (both for the certification team), a customer-facing installation guide, and the listing content (marketing docs and demo videos). Recording the demo video needs a person.

steps.title: (Optional, Store route) Submit and wait for certification
steps.detail: Certification runs two tracks, app review and listing review, covering security, performance, platform stability and installation. ServiceNow's KB says it typically takes 3-5 weeks. A third-party guide suggests planning 5-8 weeks from build completion to a live listing.

requirements.detail: A free personal developer instance works for testing. Production use requires admin access on each customer's instance.

requirements.item: OAuth 2.0 plugin active and com.snc.platform.security.oauth.is.active = true
requirements.detail: Both are on by default on new and upgraded instances.
The Redirect URL on the registry record must exactly match the Composio callback URL.
Without it no refresh token is issued.
Endpoints and client credentials are tied to the instance subdomain.
You must be a Build Partner to list on the ServiceNow Store. Membership has an annual fee.

requirements.item: Private scope, self-test results, design doc, test plan, install guide, listing assets (Store route only)

scopes.effect: Set in the Auth scope field of the registry record. It is the Composio default and the value used in common examples. It needs no review; what the token can actually do depends on the authorizing user's ServiceNow roles.

blockers.symptom: Redirect URI mismatch error during authorization
blockers.cause: The Redirect URL on the Application Registry record does not exactly match the URL Composio sends.
blockers.fix: Paste the exact Composio callback URL into the registry record's Redirect URL field.

blockers.symptom: Connection works, then fails after about 30 minutes with no refresh
blockers.cause: Refresh Token Lifespan is 0, so no refresh token was issued.
blockers.fix: Set Refresh Token Lifespan above 0 (for example 8,640,000) and reconnect.

blockers.symptom: Token request fails or returns no token
blockers.cause: OAuth is inactive on the instance, or (per one community thread) the user account did not have 'Web service access only' checked.
blockers.fix: Confirm the OAuth 2.0 plugin is active and com.snc.platform.security.oauth.is.active is true. If tokens still fail, check the user account settings.

blockers.cause: Inbound OAuth supports only Authorization Code and Resource Owner Password grants (per community source).
blockers.fix: Use the authorization code flow, which is what Composio's OAUTH2 mode uses.

blockers.symptom: Cannot publish app to the ServiceNow Store
blockers.cause: The app is in the global scope, or the publisher is not a Build Partner.
blockers.fix: Rebuild in a private scope and join the Partner Program as a Build Partner.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for ServiceNow, so you always bring your own Client ID and Secret from an Application Registry record in the target instance. Use the OAUTH2 auth config, enter the instance subdomain (endpoints are https://{subdomain}.service-now.com/oauth_auth.do and /oauth_token.do), and paste Composio's callback URL as the registry Redirect URL. Each customer instance needs its own registration and credentials.
